A.beschreibung: What your doctorate is about: the topic, the application field of semiconductor packaging and your roadmap.

B.beschreibung: Numbers, beam and light–matter interaction: the toolkit for everything that follows.

C.beschreibung: How ultrashort pulses are generated and why their time scales change ablation.

D.beschreibung: Threshold, mechanisms and how glass, silicon, metal and polymer behave in a layer stack.

E.beschreibung: Microvias, glass core and TGVs, singulation and debonding: where ultrafast lasers are needed in packaging.

F.beschreibung: Equipment, lab routines, metrology and your first own experiments.

G.beschreibung: Quality, research landscape and scientific practice: from the gap to your own question.

H.beschreibung: Scientific English for speaking, writing and reading, alongside all stages.

k21.titel: Your research topic: ultrafast lasers in packaging
k21.kurz: The topic, why packaging needs ultrafast lasers, the learning path as a map, from topic to question
k21.bezug: The compass for everything else: here you see how each chapter feeds into your research question.

k15.titel: Semiconductor packaging: from chip to system
k15.kurz: Tasks of the package, front end and back end, dicing street, dies per wafer
k15.bezug: Without knowing the application field you cannot ask a relevant research question. Here you learn what a package has to do.

k16.titel: Packaging architectures: from wire bond to chiplet
k16.kurz: Wire bond, flip chip, BGA, fan-out, 2.5D, 3D, hybrid bonding
k16.bezug: Every architecture brings its own laser steps (vias, interposers, singulation). That decides where your work can start.

k00.kurz: Powers of ten, units, logarithm, estimation, pocket calculator
k00.bezug: You will calculate fluence, threshold and throughput all the time, in your head and in the lab notebook. This is the toolkit.

k01.titel: Pulse quantities and a feel for numbers
k01.kurz: Time scales, pulse energy, peak power, fluence, intensity, photon energy
k01.bezug: With this you translate every machine setting (pulse energy, repetition rate, power) into physical quantities such as fluence.

k02.titel: Beam optics: from the laser to the focus
k02.kurz: Gaussian beam, focusing, Rayleigh length, beam quality M²
k02.bezug: Spot size and focal position set the diameter and taper of your holes.

k03.kurz: Bands, absorption, reflection, linear and nonlinear absorption
k03.bezug: Explains why copper, silicon, glass and polymer in the same package react so differently to the same pulse.

k04.kurz: Bandwidth, mode locking, chirp, CPA, amplifier architectures
k04.bezug: Pulse duration, burst and repetition rate are the levers on your machine. Here you learn where they come from.

k05.titel: Time scales and the two-temperature model
k05.kurz: Heat diffusion vs. pulse duration, electron and lattice systems, TTM
k05.bezug: Heat accumulation is the main enemy for polymers and thin layers in a package. This is the physics behind it.

k06.kurz: Multiphoton and tunnel ionization, Keldysh, avalanche, plasma
k06.bezug: Glass for interposers and glass cores absorbs only nonlinearly. Without this chapter, drilling TGVs stays a black box.

k07.kurz: Threshold, ablation depth, spallation, phase explosion, incubation, burst
k07.bezug: Threshold and ablation depth are the key quantities of your first own test series.

k08.kurz: Band gap, absorption regimes, cracking, residual stress
k08.bezug: Material classes and cracking: the basis for processing glass, silicon and ceramics in a package in a controlled way.

k17.titel: Materials and thermomechanics in the package
k17.kurz: Filled polymers, CTE mismatch, die strength, Weibull, layer stack
k17.bezug: A package stacks materials with very different thresholds and thermal expansion. Selectivity and delamination are typical research questions.

k18.titel: IC substrate, microvias and glass core
k18.kurz: Build-up layers, CO₂/UV/USP drilling, burst, top hat, TGV
k18.bezug: The core chapter: microvias and through-glass vias are processes the AG alp has already published on, and obvious candidates for your topic.

k19.titel: Separating and releasing: dicing and debonding
k19.kurz: Saw, laser grooving, stealth dicing, plasma, laser debonding
k19.bezug: Dicing, grooving and debonding are further laser steps in the back-end and possible alternatives for your topic.

k10.kurz: LIPSS, selective laser etching, Bessel beam, waveguides
k10.bezug: Selective laser etching and Bessel beams are the basis of laser-induced etching of through-glass vias.

k09.kurz: Pulse spacing, hatch, scanner, beam delivery, pulse shaping, DoE
k09.bezug: You set pulse distance, hatch and scan strategy for every experiment on the machine.

k14.titel: Everyday lab work at the USP system
k14.kurz: Safety, beam alignment, focus search, power, pulse duration and Liu evaluation as games
k14.bezug: The routines before every experiment: safety, alignment, focal position, power, threshold.

k11.kurz: Pulse duration, beam profile, uncertainty, roughness, standards, in-situ monitoring
k11.bezug: What you cannot measure properly you cannot publish: microscopy, surface parameters and standards for your results.

k22.kurz: Drilling strategies, threshold on a Si wafer, drilling and ablation series, material comparison, protocol
k22.bezug: Here, what you have learned becomes your first test plan on the machine.

k20.kurz: Measurement methods, failure mechanisms, yield, conferences, reading list
k20.bezug: Quality criteria, reading list and open questions: the transition from getting started to your own research question.

k12.kurz: Journals, conferences, reading papers, reference management, presenting
k12.bezug: Reading papers, managing literature, positioning your results: the craft of a doctorate.

k13.kurz: Numbers aloud, describing setups and graphs, abstracts, conversations
k13.bezug: Papers, conferences and talks with partners are in English. This chapter runs alongside all stages.
